cells.tense: You are the one holding many truths at once and reading how the thing in front of you is put together, and the pen is in your hand right now.
cells.ask: Take one pattern you've noticed lately and write what it's made of in plain words, no theory. One page. Then leave it alone until tomorrow.
cells.core:
Someone hands you a situation and you don't just hear the story. You see what's attached to what and which part moves first. That's what's happening right now, and it's working — the structure you're reading holds up when you test it against what's actually in front of you.

When you can see how something is built, you can say it out loud, and saying it is what lets anyone else use it. That's the live edge at the moment. Keeping it working costs something, though: the read stays useful while it's yours to test. Put it into too many hands too soon and it flattens into a slogan. Hold it a while longer and say what it's made of before you say what it means.
cells.sheetLine: You see how the thing is built, and it holds up.
cells.verb: holding many truths at once and reading how a thing is put together
cells.place: where the pattern shows itself once the content drops away

cells.tense: You will keep chasing the pattern past every version of it, and you're already living somewhere ahead of the one you're standing in.
cells.ask: Pick the pattern you're working on and stop at the first version a stranger could follow. Say it out loud once, then put it down for the rest of the day.
cells.core:
You're reading structure at a speed this moment can't hold. One shape leads to another, and then to one underneath that, until you're explaining things that haven't happened and might not. The reading is real. It's just running out past anything you could check it against, and once it's out there it isn't reading anymore — it's bracing.

What's reliable is smaller than what you're doing. It's the read that lands clean, without you having to argue for it, on something already in front of you. Not the next layer, and not the layer below that. Notice how much attention is going into futures assembled out of pure shape. The same situation has a plainer face, and you can look at it.
cells.sheetLine: You've run past the pattern into futures that haven't happened.

cells.tense: You stopped reading how things were put together, and you've been walking past surfaces as if surfaces were the whole of it.
cells.ask: Take one situation you currently explain as just how it is. Write one sentence naming something it's connected to. One link, then stop.
cells.core:
Whatever habit of reading structure you had is still in you, but it isn't coming out. Situations pass and you take them at face value — this happened, then that, done. A world made of flat separate events, each one closed by the time you leave it.

What you're without isn't cleverness. It's letting one thing connect to another and following the line a step to see where it goes. That's smaller than it sounds. One link is enough to start with, and you don't need to know where it leads. The raw material for this is the situation you already have in front of you, and only you can bring it.
cells.sheetLine: You've stopped noticing how things connect to each other.

cells.tense: You are already calling how something will go before it goes that way, and you're describing it as mood, luck, or just how things are.
cells.ask: Take one call you've made recently about how something would turn out. Write it down with the date, keep it, and look at it once the thing is over.
cells.core:
You say how a conversation will go before it starts. You know which plan will fold and where a person's story is heading, and you file it under being realistic, or under noticing things, and it doesn't count as anything you did. The reading keeps happening. You just don't sign it.

That costs you. A call you didn't write down can't be checked, and unchecked it drifts toward whatever is convenient to believe afterward. Writing it before it lands is different from carrying it quietly — one is something you can stand behind and one isn't. Keep the note. See what the record says about you.
cells.sheetLine: You already call how it goes. Try writing it down first.

attempts.check: The record supports pattern-recognition sharpened by abundance, seated in abstraction, but nothing about this person's history, temperament, or what any pattern actually is in their life — the draft must not name content. A reader could reasonably say the reading doesn't tell them what the pattern is about, which is true and stays true. The asks survive being wrong: each is one visible act, available today without money, energy, or another person on standby, and none promises an outcome. The sentence that would serve me more than them is any line praising how rare or how much they see — cut, and the cells say what attention is doing, not how special it is.
